subject: SLA amendment request: uptime baseline adjustment & monthly remedy cap
messages:
From: Shearwater Systems <contracts@shearwater.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@shearwater.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: SLA amendment request — uptime baseline and monthly cap

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re excited about moving forward with Redwood Private for our inference stack, but we need to request a scoped amendment to the standard SLA template before we sign. Our infra will be colocated and will run heavily batched, periodic workloads for model training-footprint reasons. That increases our exposure to short-term capacity variance.

Request summary:
- Uptime floor: adjust from Redwood’s standard 99.9% (hosted baseline) to 99.5% for our private/dedicated deployment.
- Monthly remedy cap: cap service credits at $25,000 per month (rather than percentage-only unlimited exposure).
- Maintenance carveouts: ask for expanded scheduled maintenance window flexibility during our monthly batch runs.

We’ve attached a short doc (Shearwater-SLA-requests.pdf) with rationale and a proposed phase-in timeline. We’d like to understand whether Redwood can accept this limited exception, and if so any required offsets (e.g., increased runbook support, telemetry access, or a pilot period).

Can you confirm whether your legal/ops teams will consider a 99.5 floor with a capped remedy? We’re trying to close procurement in July.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Contracts Manager
Shearwater Systems

[Attachment: Shearwater-SLA-requests.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Shearwater Systems <contracts@shearwater.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — uptime baseline and monthly cap

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. I looped in Laura (AM) to align on onboarding and Ben (sales/legal) will chime in on the contract offsets.

High level: we do offer scoped SLA exceptions for Dedicated/Private customers where the underlying infra or operational cadence materially changes the risk profile. Those exceptions typically require:
- a defined pilot window (3–6 months) to validate operational assumptions
- a capped monthly remedy with a mutually agreed threshold
- clear scheduled-maintenance windows and a carveout for planned batch operations
- telemetry/trace access for timely RCA (we can provide a restricted view)

As a starting point, I attached a short draft amendment (proposed-amendment-draft.docx) that outlines a 99.5 uptime floor for the Private deployment with a proposed remedy cap of $30,000/month and a 6-month pilot. We also included an option for a monthly review cadence.

If this direction looks reasonable, Ben can formalize the language and Laura will coordinate the operational runbook. We’re open to adjusting the cap and pilot length based on your risk needs.

I’ll wait for Elena’s feedback and Ben’s counter-offer.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

[Attachment: proposed-amendment-draft.docx]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@shearwater.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA amendment request — uptime baseline and monthly cap

Elena — appreciate the write-up. I’ve reviewed Marissa’s draft and chatted briefly with legal. A pragmatic counter-proposal to accelerate close while limiting commercial exposure:

Counter-proposal (high level):
- Uptime floor for Private: 99.6% (measured monthly) — we can accept slightly higher than your ask to reduce operational risk on both sides.
- Monthly remedy cap: USD 20,000 per month.
- Pilot: 3-month operational pilot to validate batch window carveouts and failover behavior.
- Carveouts: explicit third-party infra and force majeure carveouts plus scheduled maintenance windows (we propose 6 hours per month, coordinated).
- Telemetry: give Shearwater a restricted telemetry dashboard and daily incident notifications during pilot.

If Shearwater can accept 99.6% and the $20k cap, we’ll prepare contract language and an initial DocuSign packet. We can also add an SLA review clause after the pilot.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[DocuSign preview: https://docusign.example.com/embedded/abc123-DEAL-4739]

Note: this is a negotiated exception — it will only be accepted for Private/dedicated deployments with the pilot and telemetry commitments in place.

From: Elena Park <elena.park@shearwater.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA amendment request — uptime baseline and monthly cap

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the fast turn. The counter-proposal gets us most of the way there. Two items from our side before we sign:

1) Monthly cap: can you reduce to USD 15,000? That aligns with our internal risk tolerance and procurement buckets.
2) Latency: we need a P95 latency guardrail for our interactive endpoints — not just availability. Proposed metric: P95 < 250ms for 90% of traffic, measured at the ingress gateway. We’ll attach a short spreadsheet with our latency distribution (latency-metrics.xlsx).

If you can accept the $15k cap and include the latency definition in the amendment (with clear measurement method), we can move to DocuSign and schedule the pilot kickoff.

Best,
Elena Park
Contracts Manager
Shearwater Systems

[Attachment: latency-metrics.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@shearwater.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA amendment request — uptime baseline and monthly cap

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. A few clarifying points and a proposal to close quickly:

Latency metric definition (proposed):
- P95 latency measured at Redwood ingress for production traffic associated with Shearwater’s "interactive" route(s).
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window, reported monthly.
- Guardrail: P95 <= 250ms for at least 90% of sampled 30-day windows (i.e., in any calendar month, the P95 metric must be <=250ms on at least 27/30 measurement days).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows and documented third-party network outages.

Commercial: we can accept the $15k monthly cap if Shearwater commits to a 6-month pilot (instead of 3) and grants access to the restricted telemetry dashboard. The longer pilot is to ensure latency behavior stabilizes across batch windows and any host-level optimizations. After 6 months we’ll re-evaluate the floor and cap; success criteria will be latency stability and no high-severity availability incidents.

Operational notes:
- We’ll define scheduled batch windows (to be mutually agreed) and a monthly 6-hour maintenance carveout.
- If Shearwater needs guaranteed sub-250ms latency for a subset of critical endpoints, we can discuss an automatic fallback routing to hosted capacity for those routes (priced separately).

Next steps: I’ll incorporate the latency language and the 6-month pilot into the amendment and resend a DocuSign packet. Can we set a short review call next week to finalize runbook and telemetry permissions?

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[Attachment: measurement-specs.md]

From: Elena Park <elena.park@shearwater.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA amendment request — uptime baseline and monthly cap

Laura / Marissa / Ben — that all sounds reasonable. We’ll review the revised amendment when you send it and circle back during the review call next week. If you can include the fallback routing option and the telemetry dashboard access in the DocuSign packet, procurement will be able to sign within our July target.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — looking forward to the pilot.

Elena Park
Contracts Manager
Shearwater Systems
